title: AI Is Making a Mess of Nurses’ Schedules. They Say It’s a Safety Issue
key_facts: Since 2023 HCA Healthcare, the largest US hospital chain, has rolled out Timpani, an AI nurse-scheduling tool built with Palantir, at roughly 130 of its 190 locations.

Nurses who spoke to WIRED allege the tool has potentially harmed patients by leaving care teams understaffed, imbalanced and exhausted, with too few nurses or too few experienced ones on shifts, particularly Sundays, and frequent disregard of their shift preferences.
Critical care nurse Amber Retzloff says she asked for 50 specific shifts over four months and was given different ones more than half the time.

HCA spokesperson Harlow Sumerford says nursing leaders, not Timpani, make final scheduling decisions and calls claims that the tool is designed to reduce staffing at the expense of patient care misrepresentative.
HCA says Timpani schedules nurses on 1 percent of their requested days off on average.

In July a former HCA data science manager, Angelique Russell, sued, alleging she was fired in retaliation for raising concerns and that HCA routinely deleted data the tool uses; HCA has yet to formally respond in court.
HCA executive Michael Schlosser wrote in July that Timpani has cut manager scheduling hours, reduced reliance on costly contract nurses and increased retention.

National Nurses United, which represents about 10,000 of HCA's 100,000 nurses, says HCA rejected its requests for information; about 500 nurses at one psychiatric center filed a grievance that is likely headed to arbitration.
Separately, internal documents show Rayus Radiology staff complained that a Palantir-based scheduling tool linked orders to the wrong patient profiles; Rayus says the characterizations are unfair.
quote_evidence: The nurses who spoke with WIRED allege that Timpani has potentially harmed patients by causing care teams to be understaffed, imbalanced, and exhausted.
Harlow Sumerford, an HCA spokesperson, says that nursing leaders, not Timpani, make final scheduling decisions.
Leaders of National Nurses United, the labor union representing about 10,000 of HCA’s 100,000 nurses, says the company has rejected their requests for information about the technology.
why_it_matters_hint: Nurses say AI scheduling at a very large hospital chain is affecting staffing and patient safety, while HCA says humans make the final calls.
event_date: Ongoing since 2023; WIRED published 2 Oct 2026. Lawsuit filed in July 2026.
notes: Based on interviews with about six nurses and a union, plus a lawsuit HCA has not yet answered in court. HCA, Rayus and Palantir responses are included in the article. Allegations are not independently verified.
